A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NeurELA. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendix A support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot, fine-tuning, runtime, optimizer-selection, and model-complexity experiments on BBOB, BBOB-Noisy, and Protein-Docking.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GLHF evaluations and an analysis of landscape features during LDE optimization.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix A.1 retain the same population embedding, two-stage attention architecture, multitask neuroevolution objective, zero-shot integration, and fine-tuning procedure.

E1.justification: Figure 3 adds GLHF as an unseen MetaBBO task environment on the same three problem suites. MELBA was already evaluated in v1's Figure 3 despite being omitted from its accompanying prose. The new Rastrigin case study uses existing BBOB coverage.

E2.justification: The landscape-feature comparators remain Original and ELA, including within the added GLHF task. GLHF is an additional recipient MetaBBO algorithm. The evolution-strategy alternatives and MLP controls also retain their membership; DeepELA remains related work.

E3.justification: The new Section 4.3 introduces a protocol that records LDE populations on 10-dimensional Rastrigin, labels exploration versus exploitation using a mutation-factor threshold of 0.5, and projects features into two dimensions using PCA. Previously specified splits, metrics, and NeurELA training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3 and Figure 5 investigate whether NeurELA features distinguish exploration from exploitation better than ELA features. This adds a focused representation-analysis case study. Existing noise-generalization, evolution-strategy, and model-complexity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies ten LDE optimization runs for the feature-analysis case study. Existing reporting remains unchanged: fifty independent evaluation runs in Equation 3 and ten meta-training runs with 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals for Figure 3. No increase in replication of existing experiments is stated.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds GLHF NeurELA scores of 1.27, 1.43, and 1.37 on BBOB, BBOB-Noisy, and Protein-Docking, versus ELA's 0.89, 0.95, and 1.05. Existing entries and other quantitative plots are retained. Figure 5 adds qualitative feature-separation findings. Section 4.1 extends consistent-superiority wording to Protein-Docking, although its retained LDE result favors ELA, 2.44 versus 2.15.

T1.justification: The task-space definition, objectives, relative-performance formula, and attention computations in Equations 1–6 remain unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims remain automatic landscape-feature extraction through attention, multitask neuroevolution, transfer to unseen MetaBBO tasks, and efficient fine-tuning. The abstract and introduction retain these contributions, and the conclusion preserves their scope.

C2.justification: The new case study attributes performance to features that separate exploration and exploitation and help the policy balance them. The generalization discussion expands beyond noise robustness. Meanwhile, v2 removes the reduced-interpretability limitation and symbolic-regression discussion from the limitations and conclusion, retaining the training-efficiency concern.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents function-evaluation budgets of 20,000 for the standard low-level/BBOB-Noisy settings and 1,000 for Protein-Docking. These are newly disclosed settings, without evidence of changed budgets. It also adds an anonymous code-access link in the abstract while retaining the GitHub pointer in Appendix A.4.

R1.justification: Section 2 sharpens the existing comparison with learned ELA approaches, adding the distinction that NeurELA needs no predefined dimensional upper bound. GLHF, MELBA, and PCA references are added. The Prager comparative-study, explainable-AI, and symbolic-regression references are removed; DeepELA itself remains cited.

P1.justification: Localized revisions merge the separate DeepELA discussion into Landscape Analysis, insert Section 4.3, renumber the in-depth study, and revise the limitations and conclusion. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact. Some in-depth research-question labels retain their old numbering.

P2.justification: Figure 1's radar chart expands to include MELBA and GLHF, and Figure 3 adds GLHF groups. A new PCA visualization becomes Figure 5. Existing ablation plots are relocated and renumbered, with corresponding text reflow; the appendix landscape plots are only renumbered.

improvement.justification: The additional GLHF evidence, feature visualization, and explicit evaluation budgets improve empirical support and transparency. However, v2 removes an interpretability caveat that the qualitative PCA study does not resolve, and its expanded Protein-Docking superiority wording overlooks the LDE counterexample in Figure 3. These gains and weakened qualifications leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
